difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. The stimulus argues that the new packaging caused an increase in sales, but the correct answer introduces a simple confounder (change in retail distribution) that could explain the rise just as well.
stimulus: A marketing director at a consumer goods company noticed that sales of the company's laundry detergent increased by 30 percent in the six months following the introduction of a new, more eco-friendly packaging design. The director concludes that the new packaging design was responsible for the increase in sales.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many consumers report that they prefer the old packaging design to the new one.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new packaging design cost 15 percent less to produce than the old packaging design.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The company's primary competitor introduced a nearly identical packaging design two years before the company did.

choices.label: D
choices.text: During the same six-month period, the company doubled its shelf space in supermarkets nationwide, making the detergent far more visible to consumers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Market research shows that consumers increasingly prefer eco-friendly products.

explanations.correct: D provides an alternative explanation for the 30 percent sales increase. If the company doubled its shelf space during the same period, that retail expansion—not the new packaging—could be the primary driver of the sales increase. This undermines the director's causal claim.
explanations.A: Irrelevant. Consumer preference for the old design would undermine the packaging change as a driver, but the stimulus is about a sales increase, not satisfaction. Many sold products can still come from a less-preferred package.
explanations.B: Irrelevant to the causal claim. Production cost has no bearing on whether the packaging design drove consumer purchases.
explanations.C: Out of scope. The competitor's earlier packaging does not explain why this company's sales rose after its own packaging change, nor does it offer an alternative cause.
explanations.E: Supports the director's conclusion. If consumers prefer eco-friendly products, the eco-friendly packaging becomes a more plausible driver of the sales increase, so this strengthens rather than weakens the argument.
